text:
The bowers where I see,

in dreams, the most varied

songbirds are lips, and they are

your musical whispered words.


Your eyes, enthroned in heaven,

fall at last desperately,

oh God!, into my funereal mind

like starlight upon a veil.


Oh, your heart... I sigh when I wake

and sleep to dream until daybreak

in the truth that gold can never buy

and in the trifles that it could.

translation.title: To...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the dream-bower imagery and the contrast between priceless truth and purchasable trifles.
